title: Risk Management Topics - Fraud Monitoring Phase 2
pinpoint: Effective Dates; Who Phase 2 applies to; obligations paragraph
summary: Phase 1 (2026-03-20) covers all ODFIs and non-consumer Originators/TPSPs/TPSs with 2023 volume >=6m; Phase 2 (June 19, practically June 22, 2026) covers all other non-consumer Originators, TPSPs and TPSs. Each must keep risk-based procedures to identify entries unauthorized or authorized under False Pretenses, reviewed at least annually; pre-screening of every entry not required.

title: Summary of Upcoming Rule Changes
summary: Lists 2026-03-20 fraud monitoring Phase 1 and new Company Entry Descriptions PAYROLL/PURCHASE; 2026-06-22 Phase 2; 2026-09-18 funds availability for non-same-day credits and IAT definition; 2027 contact registry/character set/IAT; 2027-09-17 Same Day ACH limit $10m; 2028-03-17 new return reason R90 (sanctions).

title: Third Parties in the ACH Network
pinpoint: Definitions of TPSP, TPS, Nested TPS; audit paragraph
summary: TPSP provides ACH-processing services on behalf of another party and may or may not transmit entries. A TPS is a TPSP acting for an Originator without a direct Originator-ODFI agreement. A Nested TPS originates through another TPS. TPSs perform annual Rules Compliance Audits and risk assessments.

title: Third-Party Sender Roles and Responsibilities (rule page)
pinpoint: Definition of Nested TPS; Risk Assessment; Origination Agreements
summary: Nested TPS is a TPS with an agreement with another TPS to act for an Originator and no direct ODFI agreement. Every TPS must do its own risk assessment and cannot rely on another TPS's audit. ODFI-TPS agreement must state whether nesting is allowed; TPSs perform and warrant ODFI obligations.

title: RMAG Originator Essentials
pinpoint: Sections: Authorization (2.3); Returns (2.12, 3.8, 8.119); Notification of Change (2.12, 3.9, App. 5); Reversals (2.9, 2.10); SEC Code Usage
summary: Unauthorized returns are R05, R07, R10, R11, R29, R51; unauthorized rate may not exceed 0.5%. NOC changes within six banking days or before the next entry, whichever is later. Reversals within five banking days; failure to fund is not an error. Corporate SEC codes: two-day return; consumer: extended return (60 days). Burden of proof of authorization is on the Originator.

title: End-User Briefing: Limitation of Warranty Claims
pinpoint: Consumer Account and Non-Consumer Account paragraphs
summary: RDFI breach-of-authorization warranty claims against the ODFI are limited: consumer accounts, first 95 calendar days from settlement of the first unauthorized entry always covered, otherwise two years from settlement of the entry; non-consumer accounts, one year from settlement. ODFIs usually charge these back to the Originator contractually.

title: The Rules Behind Reinitiated Entries
pinpoint: Reinitiation conditions; formatting; cites Nacha Rules Subsection 2.12.4.2 (2021 Rules p. OR 37)
summary: Reinitiation permitted only if returned for insufficient/uncollected funds, returned for stop payment and separately authorized by the Receiver after the return, or the Originator/ODFI has taken corrective action. Reinitiated entries go in a separate batch with Company Entry Description exactly 'RETRY PYMT' and identical Company Name, Company ID and Amount.

title: Reinitiation limits (two reinitiations within 180 days; R10 for violations; effective 2015-09-18) - search-indexed bank and association summaries
pinpoint: Search-result text only; Nacha Rules Subsection 2.12.4 not read first-hand
summary: Secondary sources agree an R01/R09 return may be reinitiated at most two times after the original (three presentments) within 180 days of the original settlement date, and that RDFIs may use R10 to return a reinitiation that violates the rule. Not verified against the rulebook text.

title: WEB Proof of Authorization Industry Practices
pinpoint: Search-result text citing Nacha Operating Rules Article Two, Subsection 2.3.2.7 (not fetched; one bank letter cites 2.3.2.5)
summary: Search-indexed text: Originator must retain the original or a copy of each written authorization, or a readily and accurately reproducible Record of any other form of authorization, for two years from the termination or revocation of the authorization. Subsection number differs between sources.

title: 12 CFR 1005.2 Definitions (Regulation E)
summary: Account means a demand deposit, savings or other consumer asset account held by a financial institution and established primarily for personal, family or household purposes; consumer means a natural person. Business (sponsor or charity) accounts are outside Regulation E.

title: 12 CFR 1005.10 Preauthorized transfers (Regulation E)
summary: Preauthorized EFTs from a consumer account require written authorization signed or similarly authenticated, with a copy to the consumer; consumer may stop payment by notice three business days before; varying amounts require notice at least 10 days before unless consumer elects range-based notice.

title: UCC 4A-108 Relationship to Electronic Fund Transfer Act
summary: Article 4A does not apply to a funds transfer any part of which is governed by the EFTA; remittance-transfer exception; EFTA controls in conflict. Business-to-business wires and ACH credit transfers not involving consumer accounts are therefore Article 4A transfers.

title: UCC 4A-104 Funds transfer definitions
summary: Funds transfer is the series of transactions beginning with the originator's payment order made to pay the beneficiary, completed by acceptance by the beneficiary's bank. The fetched page does not show official comments on ACH; that ACH credit transfers are covered and debit transfers excluded is from memory of the official comment (unverified).

title: UCC 4A-402 Obligation of sender to pay receiving bank
summary: Sender's obligation to pay is excused if the funds transfer is not completed by acceptance by the beneficiary's bank; amounts paid that the sender was not obliged to pay must be refunded with interest (money-back guarantee).

title: UCC 4A-404 Obligation of beneficiary's bank to pay and give notice
summary: On acceptance the beneficiary's bank must pay the beneficiary and, for payment to an account, notify the beneficiary by midnight of the next funds-transfer business day. Acceptance plus confirmation is the strongest evidence of receipt for a wire or ACH credit.

title: UCC 4A-207 Misdescription of beneficiary
summary: Where name and account number identify different persons, the beneficiary's bank may rely on the number; a non-bank originator bears the loss if it had notice (e.g., signed agreement) that payment may be made on the number alone. Supports destination-proof (account ownership) evidence before payment.

title: UCC 4A-302 Obligations of receiving bank in execution
summary: Unless instructed by the sender, a receiving bank may not collect its charges by forwarding a payment order for the amount less charges, nor instruct later banks to do so. Domestic Article 4A wires therefore should arrive gross; deductions arise mainly on international legs (SHA/BEN) outside Article 4A.

title: UCC 4-406 Customer's duty to discover and report unauthorized signature or alteration
summary: Customer must examine statements with reasonable promptness; preclusion and comparative fault allocate check-fraud losses; one-year absolute bar. Bank agreements commonly shift loss to customers who decline positive pay (contract practice, not statute).

title: UCC 4-404 Bank not obliged to pay check more than six months old
summary: A bank is under no obligation to pay an uncertified check presented more than six months after its date but may pay in good faith and charge the account. Staleness does not cancel the check; a stop payment or positive-pay void is needed.

title: UCC 3-310 Effect of instrument on obligation
summary: Taking an uncertified check suspends the underlying obligation until dishonor, payment or certification; payment discharges it to the extent of the check. Voiding the instrument therefore does not by itself discharge any underlying obligation that exists.

title: Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act (2016), official text with comments
issuer: Uniform Law Commission (copy hosted by Maine Legislature)
pinpoint: Sec. 102 comment (business-to-business, 'Fifteen states'); Sec. 201(4); Secs. 302-304 and comments; Sec. 1005(a)-(d) and comment
summary: Debt of a business association presumed abandoned 3 years after obligation arises; custody priority: owner's last-known address state (restating Texas v. New Jersey), then holder's domicile. A record of unpaid debt is prima facie evidence, rebuttable by showing a check was issued without consideration (c)(6) or voided [not later than 90 days]/[within a reasonable time] for a valid business reason in a contemporaneous record (c)(8). Comment: 15 states have some B2B exemption.

title: Texas v. New Jersey, 379 U.S. 674 (1965)
pinpoint: Opinion not fetched; rule taken from RUUPA Sec. 302 comment (EV-C-021) and NAAG summary (EV-C-024)
summary: Primary rule: intangible debt escheats to the state of the creditor's last-known address in the debtor's records; secondary rule: if no address or that state does not provide for escheat, to the debtor's state of incorporation, subject to later claim by the primary state.

title: Delaware v. Pennsylvania (No. 145 Orig., decided 2023-02-28)
pinpoint: Search results only (opinion PDF not read; Justia returned 403)
summary: Held MoneyGram agent checks and teller's checks are 'similar written instruments' under the Federal Disposition Act (escheat to state of purchase), displacing the Texas v. New Jersey rules for those instruments. Ordinary checks drawn by a DAF sponsor on its own account are not money orders/teller's checks, so the common-law priority rules continue to apply (interpretation).

title: Supreme Court Report: Delaware v. Pennsylvania, 145 Orig.
summary: Describes the primary rule (escheat to the state of the payee/creditor's address) and secondary rule (holder's state of incorporation when the address is unknown), and that Congress abrogated those rules for instruments within the Federal Disposition Act. (The fetched summary named the 1965 case 'Texas v. New York', apparently a page or extraction error.)

title: Batch 34C: escheat of voided DAF grant checks (state statute table)
jurisdiction: US: RUUPA, DE, CA, NY, MA, WA, UCC
pinpoint: Section 1.1 table; Section 1.2 items 1-5; source table B01-B15
summary: Prior pass (marked [F] fetched there, not re-fetched here except RUUPA) records: Delaware 12 Del. C. 1175(b)(6) consideration defence but no void defence; Washington RCW 63.30.610(3)(f),(h) both defences; California CCP 1520 3-year catch-all, no defence found; NY APL 1315(1-a) covers checks for goods or services only and NY OSC says no B2B exemption; Massachusetts c.200A s.5 3 years. No DAF enforcement history found.

title: Business-to-business unclaimed property exemptions (state groupings and recent repeals)
issuer: Alston & Bird (2022); The Tax Adviser (2015); Wipfli (2026) - search results
summary: About 15 states have some B2B exemption (Alston 2022). Broad exemptions reported for Kansas, Maryland, Ohio, Virginia; partial for Indiana, Iowa, Michigan, Wisconsin; Illinois eliminated its exemption; Wipfli (Aug 2026) reports Arizona legislation repealing its B2B exemption. Ohio's exemption is described as covering payments between business associations for goods sold or services performed.

title: Publication 1771, Charitable Contributions - Substantiation and Disclosure Requirements (Rev. 11-2023)
pinpoint: pp. 2-4 (Contemporaneous Written Acknowledgment; Goods and Services; Token and Membership Benefits Exceptions); p. 6 (Written Disclosure Statement)
summary: Acknowledgment must state organization name, amount of any monetary contribution, description of non-cash property, and whether goods or services were provided (with good faith FMV estimate). Membership benefits for annual payment of $75 or less may be disregarded. Quid pro quo payments over $75 require a written disclosure statement; deduction limited to excess over FMV.

title: Charitable contributions - quid pro quo contributions
summary: Quid pro quo contribution is a payment partly a contribution and partly for goods or services; disclosure required when the payment exceeds $75; penalty $10 per contribution, capped at $5,000 per fundraising event or mailing, absent reasonable cause; deduction limited to excess over FMV.

title: 26 CFR 1.170A-1(h) Payments in exchange for consideration
summary: A payment in exchange for goods or services is a contribution only if the payer intends to and does pay more than FMV; deduction limited to the excess; 'in consideration for' means the payer receives or expects goods or services; donor may rely on donee's good-faith estimate in the 170(f)(8) acknowledgment or 6115 statement.

title: 26 U.S.C. 170(f)(8) and (f)(18)
summary: Acknowledgment must state the amount of cash contributed. A DAF contribution is deductible only if the donor obtains a contemporaneous written acknowledgment from the sponsoring organization that it has exclusive legal control over the assets contributed.

title: Rev. Rul. 67-246, 1967-2 C.B. 104
pinpoint: Not fetched; cited from general knowledge
summary: Establishes that payments to charities in connection with admissions or other privileges are presumed not to be gifts except to the extent they exceed the value of the benefits received, and that the charity should state the deductible portion. Principle later codified in 1.170A-1(h) and 6115.

title: Donor-covered processing fee receipt practice (Bloomerang 'Ask an expert'; Blackbaud Donor Cover help)
summary: Industry sources state that a voluntary donor-elected fee coverage paid to the charity is part of the gift and receipts show the full combined amount; a mandatory fee is not a gift. Blackbaud says 100% of the payment goes to the organization and the full amount is deductible.

title: Dispute timeframes
source_type: acquirer documentation of card network rules
effective_date: current (Visa US/Canada 9-day response for disputes from 2025-07-21)
summary: Visa and Mastercard: cardholder/issuer chargeback window generally 120 days from transaction date, up to 540 days in some cases (e.g., delayed delivery); merchant response 9 days (Visa US/Canada, disputes from 2025-07-21) or 18 days, 40 days for Mastercard; pre-arbitration and final stages extend further.

title: Visa Core Rules and Mastercard Chargeback Guide time limits (secondary summaries)
pinpoint: Search snippets only; network rulebooks not read
summary: Visa dispute processed no later than 120 calendar days from Transaction Processing Date or from expected delivery, capped at 540 days; Mastercard 120 days generally from Central Site Business Date. Official rulebooks not fetched; acquirer agreements govern merchant exposure.

title: Prevent debit blocks and failed fundings (R29) with BILL ACH IDs
summary: Payment providers that fund payouts by ACH debit from the customer's account ask customers to allowlist the provider's ACH Company IDs with their bank; otherwise debits return R29. Some banks block by Company ID, others by amount threshold.

title: Balance and Transaction Reporting Standard (ANSI X9.121) and ISO 20022 camt.052/053/054 (secondary sources)
issuer: ANSI/X9 blog; Minneapolis Fed Remittance Coalition; RBS translation guide (search snippets)
source_type: standards catalogue and professional sources (search snippets)
summary: X9 BTRS (ANSI X9.121, 2016 revision) succeeds BAI2 with the same record structure and standardized type codes. ISO 20022 camt.052 is the intraday account report, camt.053 the end-of-day statement, camt.054 the debit/credit notification. Bank-specific availability and latency not established.

title: NACHA ISO 20022 Guide: camt.053 returns
pinpoint: Search result title only; not fetched
summary: Nacha publishes mapping guides between ACH return information and ISO 20022 camt.053, indicating returns can be carried in camt statements; field mapping not read here.

title: Chariot Account FAQs (Chariot Deposit Account)
summary: The Chariot Deposit Account is a bank account legally owned by the nonprofit and hosted by Column N.A., Member FDIC; partner grantmakers' funds are deposited electronically when the grantmaker approves; non-partner grants continue by mailed check; free to claim and transfer out.

title: What are Grant Payments? (PayPal help article help883)
pinpoint: Help article sections: eligibility, accept/decline, expiration, fees
summary: Grantmakers (DAFs, community foundations) send grants to confirmed PayPal charity accounts; the charity accepts or declines; accepted funds available within a day; grants expire on a grantmaker-set date and the grantmaker resends by other methods; no receiving fees.

title: moov-io/ach documentation: Returns
summary: Return entries carry an Addenda99 with ReturnCode, OriginalTrace (trace number of the original entry), OriginalDFI and AddendaInformation; the return entry carries its own new trace number.

title: ACH File Details (Nacha ACH Developer Guide)
summary: Trace number is assigned by the ODFI in ascending sequence and uniquely identifies each entry within a batch and file; the page fetched does not show return (99) or NOC (98) addenda layouts.

title: What it costs (Giving Account administrative fee)
summary: Annual administrative fee 0.60% or $100, whichever is greater, tiered under $5m; fee examples computed on an average annual balance. Averaging method (daily) and billing frequency not confirmed.

title: Sponsor fee schedules stating average-daily-balance bases (NPT; GlobalTrust; Idaho CF)
pinpoint: NPT row ('admin fee blended schedule on average daily balance'); b50-04-giving-circles.md Idaho CF row; b45n33-01 GlobalTrust
summary: Prior research records several sponsors that state fees on average daily balance (NPT, GlobalTrust Funds, Idaho Community Foundation '2.0% of average daily fund balance with a minimum fee of $500'). Not re-fetched in this pass.

title: Batch 33: voided grant checks and rails (Fidelity, GiveClear, BlueGive 90-day void)
summary: Published national-sponsor void rules are 90 days with funds returned to the giving account (Fidelity, GiveClear, BlueGive); no sponsor states an escheat treatment; Vanguard and NPT keep discretion.

title: DAF Industry Report 2026-11 (disbursement rail camps)
summary: Four disbursement camps: Fidelity EFT/Stripe, PayPal Grant Payments (NPT up to $250k, Vanguard up to $10m), Ren RDE, Chariot Disbursements (GiveClear, Daffy, Founders Pledge, Groundswell, Charityvest). PayPal Giving Fund is a separate charity, not the Grant Payments rail.

title: Request for Comment - Return Efficiencies - Return Time Frames
summary: Nacha request for comment proposing an additional shortened return timeframe, with a listed effective date of 2028-09-15; not adopted rule as of search.

title: ACH Network Risk and Enforcement Topics (rule page)
summary: Search-indexed text: the rule makes explicit the prohibition on reinitiating outside the limited circumstances in Subsection 2.12.4 and lets RDFIs use R10 for a return resulting from a violation of the Reinitiation Rule.

title: Nacha Return entry addenda (type 99) layout - study guide
summary: Return addenda: Addenda Type Code 99, Return Reason Code positions 04-06, Original Entry Trace Number 07-21, then Date of Death and Original Receiving DFI Identification; NOC addenda type 98 with Change Code 04-06 and Corrected Data. To be confirmed against the Nacha rulebook Appendix Three.
